subject: Unplanned inference latency and 5xx from QuantCore — dedicated pool pressure
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@quantcore.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: claire.huang@quantcore.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: High latency spikes + growing 5xx rate — affecting checkout flows

Vanessa —

We are seeing a sudden jump in tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors from the Redwood dedicated pool serving our models in us-west. Checkout latency on our side has doubled and a few merchants reported failed authorizations. Our ops team captured traces and metrics (attached). This started ~07:40 PST and is ongoing.

Can someone from Redwood confirm whether this is a platform-side saturation or if this is an application-level change on our end? We are in a high-traffic window and need an ETA on mitigation.

Attachments:
- quantcore-request-logs-clip-20261122.txt (3.2 MB, text)
- quantcore-metrics-snapshot-20261122.png (750 KB, image)

Thanks,
Ethan
Director of Engineering, QuantCore
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: ethan.shaw@quantcore.com
Cc: claire.huang@quantcore.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:21:45 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency spikes + growing 5xx rate — affecting checkout flows

Ethan —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments, they help a lot. Im escalating to our on-call infra and well triage immediately. Two quick asks while we investigate:

1) Can you confirm if you recently changed model size, batch settings, or request rate limits on your side in the last hour?
2) Please hold on any rollout to your production model until we clear the cause.

Im looping in Rishi and Jonas from our capacity and SRE teams. I will come back with an initial root-cause or a mitigation path within 30 minutes.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:28:10 -0800
Subject: Fwd: High latency spikes + growing 5xx rate — QuantCore (urgent)

Team — forwarding QuantCores evidence. They report tail latency doubling and 5xxs starting ~07:40 PST. They are on a dedicated GPU pool in us-west and have reserved throughput (QC-9876).

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: run a headroom check and cross-tenant spillover analysis. Any sign of slot exhaustion or noisy neighbor?
- Jonas: look at kernel/driver error rates and queue depths for the us-west dedicated pool; capture recent autoscaler logs.
- Marissa: please prepare a short client-facing summary and a concrete mitigation option (burst authorization, temporary downgrade to smaller model, or routing to fallback region).

Priority: this is impacting merchant checkouts. If we cant get an app-level explanation from QuantCore within 20m, we should be ready to request emergency burst capacity.

Vanessa
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:49:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency spikes + growing 5xx rate — QuantCore (urgent)

Quick status update:
- Headroom: the us-west dedicated pool for QuantCore shows sustained 92% GPU utilization across the last 15 minutes; KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% correlating with increased sequence lengths in their request sample.
- Queueing: NVTX traces show queue depths growing beyond our continuous-batching thresholds; several evictions recorded that map to 5xx errors (OOM/timeout).
- Noisy neighbor: were seeing a short burst from an adjacent tenant aligned temporally, but not sufficient alone to explain the headroom rise.

Next steps:
1) Recommend immediate temporary burst authorization of +25% reserved throughput to QuantCore (pre-approved per emergency playbook) to relieve tail latency while we free up slots.
2) Start routing a small % of QC traffic to a warm fallback region (us-east) with a smaller-model variant (approx 4% expected quality delta).
3) Ops to purge stale KV prefixes that are consuming cache (low-risk) — I will coordinate.

I can enable the burst within 10 minutes if leadership signs off. Jonas, please add anything else you see.

— Rishi
Head of Capacity, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ceo@redwood.ai, cto@redwood.ai, claire.huang@quantcore.com, ethan.shaw@quantcore.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency spikes + growing 5xx rate — QuantCore (urgent)

Status and recommendation for execs and QuantCore:

Summary: QuantCore experienced a rapid tail-latency and 5xx surge starting 07:40 PST caused by a combination of increased request sequence length (client-side) and reduced effective KV hit-rate. The us-west dedicated GPU pool is at ~92% utilization with queueing-induced OOM/timeouts. A small noisy-neighbor burst contributed but is not the primary root cause.

Recommended immediate actions (we initiated these at 08:52 PST):
- Temporary burst authorization: +25% reserved throughput for QuantCore for 2 hours (reduces queue depth and 5xxs).
- Traffic split: route 10% of requests to us-east warm fallback with smaller-model variant; monitoring for quality delta.
- KV cleanup: ops performing targeted purge of stale prefixes (nonblocking).
- Client ask: QuantCore to hold model rollouts and confirm no increase in request concurrency or prompt lengths.

Impact: merchant checkout errors reduced by ~67% in the first 8 minutes post-burst; average p95 latency dropped from 850ms to 320ms but tail (p99) still elevated — we continue to monitor.

Actions for execs:
- Approval: request from Operations for emergency burst (+25% for 2 hours) — recommend sign-off to avoid SLA failures.
- Follow-up: propose a post-incident capacity review with QuantCore next week to adjust reservation sizing and implement predictive headroom alerts.

Attachments: quantcore-metrics-snapshot-20261122.png (evidence), JIRA QCORE-4521 created.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability (on-call)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: ethan.shaw@quantcore.com, claire.huang@quantcore.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Resolved: QuantCore checkout impact — immediate relief applied and next steps

Ethan / Claire —

Short update: we applied the emergency +25% burst at 08:52 PST, split 10% traffic to us-east with the smaller-model fallback, and completed KV cleanup. Immediate errors declined and p95/p99 improved but we will continue monitoring through the evening.

Next steps we agreed with QuantCore:
- Stand by on the burst for 2 hours (auto-expire).
- Schedule a capacity-sizing review early next week to align reservation to peak profile and add predictive alerts for KV-hit drops and sequence-length anomalies.
- Follow-up RCA (including noisy neighbor correlation and potential scheduler tweaks) to be delivered by 2026-11-24 EOD.

Thanks for the rapid coordination. Ill keep you posted on the monitoring dashboard and will escalate immediately if anything regresses.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
